title: A Quantitative Assembly of Smale Horseshoes on the 2-Sphere
content: Let \( S^{2} \) carry a fixed north–south Morse–Smale diffeomorphism \( f_{0} \). Finitely many admissible Smale horseshoe modules, placed in pairwise disjoint disks in a narrow equatorial belt, are assembled along the edges of a geometrically planar realizable gluing graph. The vertices are all Markov rectangles of the modules; the adjacency matrix records every allowed transition. Each edge is realized by a finite-length latitudinal tube. On the tube core the time-1 flow of the longitudinal field is an axial rotation, isometric for the round metric, and acts on the image of the source collar under the module map; a compactly supported, orientation-preserving \( C^{1} \) correction then matches collar boundaries. Geometric planar realizability requires cyclic order at each module, a bound on out-degree by the number of geometric exit slots, and pairwise disjoint tubes. Once rectangle order and slot counts are fixed, these three conditions are the hypotheses under which pre-transports commute, the gap \( \gamma \) is read from inter-tube distance, and \( \nu_{G} \) is independent of \( |E| \). If the graph is fully admissible, the assembled map \( h_{G} \) leaves invariant a compact set \( \Lambda_{G} \) contained in the union of rectangle interiors and prescribed collars. The set is uniformly hyperbolic with explicit constants \( \nu_{G}>1 \) and \( \theta_{G}<1 \), locally \( C^{1} \) structurally stable, and semi-conjugate to the subshift of finite type of the adjacency matrix, the semi-conjugacy being a conjugacy on a dense \( G_{\delta} \) subset. The topological entropy is \( \log\lambda_{G} \), where \( \lambda_{G} \) is the spectral radius of that matrix on the full vertex set. These conclusions are the Property Transfer Principle. Two equatorial realizations check the geometric bounds: the complete directed graph on two vertices with loops, and a directed 3-cycle with a single loop. A checklist records when the same statements apply to a two-dimensional map or return map, with polar escape replaced by a trapping region.
